answer: A jade observatory gives each certified processor a daily compute allowance. Its hardware key marks one vertex in the registry, and signed task receipts include a monotonic usage counter. The verifier totals usage across every wallet using that device and rejects reused counter ranges. A tide of aliases on one chip shares one allowance; extra capacity needs more certified chips and operating expense. This requires an unclonable device identifier, rollback-resistant counters and global accounting. Attested code alone is insufficient, and compromised hardware vendors could undermine the cap.
